questions.q: Read the hadith 'The Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe' (Bukhari and Muslim). Draw two lessons.
questions.a: 1) Guard your speech; 2) do not harm others with your actions.

questions.q: The text of a hadith is called the ...
Hadith reading card on the pupil PDF for 'Allah is kind and loves kindness in all things' (Bukhari and Muslim, from Aishah): source, narrator, key words, two lessons, one action this week.
questions.a: Source Bukhari and Muslim; narrator Aishah; key words kind, loves, all things; lessons: be gentle in everything, Allah loves it; action: pupils' own

questions.q: Extend: what should you do with a forwarded 'hadith' you cannot find a source for?
questions.a: Do not share it; ask a teacher or check a reliable collection.

questions.q: Stretch: why is reading a hadith without the scholars risky?
questions.a: You may misunderstand words, context or how it fits with other texts.
A) The chain of narrators. Isnad is the chain; matn is the text.

questions.q: Think again: what do you check before sharing a 'hadith'?
questions.a: Its source and authenticity, and what scholars say it means.
